鬼滅の刃 [Kimetsu no Yaiba] #13

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba, Vol. 13

Koyoharu Gotouge

4.52
17,628 ratings719 reviews
Rate this book
In Taisho-era Japan, Tanjiro Kamado is a kindhearted boy who makes a living selling charcoal. But his peaceful life is shattered when a demon slaughters his entire family. His little sister Nezuko is the only survivor, but she has been transformed into a demon herself! Tanjiro sets out on a dangerous journey to find a way to return his sister to normal and destroy the demon who ruined his life.

The strange shape-shifting demons Hatengu and Gyokko attack Tanjiro and his friends in the hidden village of swordsmiths. The Mist Hashira, Muichiro Tokito, engages the demons, but he’ll need some help from Tanjiro and another Demon Slayer, Genya. It’s bad enough that they have to fight two upper-rank demons, but can they handle a foe who can split itself into four separate bodies and regenerate almost instantly?

January 9, 2026
One of my favourite battles, it deserves to receive a 5 star rating!

What I loved the most about this Upper Moon was how it not has a single body but multiple. He splits up every time his head gets cut of. Even better is the fact how they all represent the four core emotions! This demon not only has multiple bodies with different abilities and weapons they fight with but also different appearances and personalities. I think that makes this battle so exciting. It's also incredibly difficult to find out what the weak point actually is to kill this one. If Tanjirou wouldn't have been there they probably would have all died. Such a sneaky demon, I love it! What I love the most about this demon though is how he is a reference to the Japanese folklore creature known as Tengu.

I had a hard time to understood Tokitou's past the first time around 'cause it was so foggy, but I understood it the second time around. One also gets a look at Genya's past, revealing his reasons for trying to become a pillar so desperately.

The Love Hashira, Kanroji, also appears but not for long. Although I think she will have a longer appearance in the next volume.

'I'm sorry, aniki. I'm going to die without ever apologizing. You smiling at me... is too good of a thing to flash before my eyes.'
"Genyaaaaa!! Don't ever give up!! Aren't you gonna become a Hashira?! Genya Shinazugawa!!"

Can I just start my review and end it by saying that I love Genya Shinazugawa and his relationship with Tanjiro Kamado with everything in me? Because I love it. With everything in me.

Tanjiro's an incredibly easy character to love and root for, Genya isn't. The first thing we saw him do in the story was attack a girl and wherever he had shown up, he was being mean, especially to Tanjiro. But Tanjiro's heart was too pure to give up on Genya. Despite their initial differences, he thought of Genya as a friend and was happy to reassure him that he was the best and to assist him in their fight against the demons. It ended with Tanjiro saving Genya and Genya saving Tanjiro - it was the perfect way to show how much they actually cared for one another and I loved it so much.

Volume 13 is also the volume where we get to know Genya more deeply than just a snappy teenager. We already knew that Genya and one of the Hashiras were related, but we had no idea what had separated them. It was all revealed here and, honestly, despite already knowing everything from the anime, I wasn't ready for the emotional impact of that flashback.

"Murderer! You murderer!"

I cried, of course I cried. This was one of the greatest tragedies in Demon Slayer and I hate that such a traumatic thing had to happen to the Shinazugawa brothers. They had been such a happy family. A poor one, an incomplete one and a little bit broken, but happy nonetheless, and of course something had to happen to take this happiness away. It hasn't just taken something away from the brothers and torn them apart, it had destroyed something deep inside them and left them hurt and broken for years. Now Genya's whole goal is to become a Hashira just to have an opportunity to meet his dearest brother, to face him and to apologize, desperate to reconcile and be a family again, but before he can do so he has to survive in a fight against an Upper Rank demon.

If you know me, you know how much I love the sibling stories, especially ones where the siblings love each other so much so that they are ready for every sacrifice for each other's sake. Sanemi Shinazugawa is a reluctant one, acting all mean and violent, keeping his distance from his brother, but I believe that deep down he cares for Genya so much that he doesn't know how to express it. I mean, there is nobody else that they can call their family now. It's just the two of them, against the world. He will come around, I am sure of it! We just need to be patient, Genya! ☺️

P.S. Little Sanemi's smile was as warm as the sun 😭

Muichiro: 'A child... that's a swordsmith. He must be an apprentice. Helping him is a low priority.'
Tanjiro in a flashback: "Helping others often ends up helping yourself."
Muichiro: *stops in his tracks and jumps to save the low priority child*

I love how impactful Tanjiro is on everyone he meets, especially the Hashiras. That's how the MC should be written! They should not only move the story forward, they should be impactful on everybody and everything, one way or another. Tanjiro's a great example of this. Muichiro wasn't someone who would risk his life for somebody he considered "low priority" or, worse, "no priority", but the meeting with Tanjiro changed that. The situation everybody was in was incredibly bad, there was danger lurking everywhere, everything getting destroyed and everyone getting killed left and right and Muichiro as a Hashira should be in the center of it, fighting the Upper Rank demon, but he decided to stop and save the kid that was in danger. That's how a Hashira should act from the very beginning, but I do like how Muichiro's behavior changed after the meeting with Tanjiro.

P.S. Let's not think how many people got injured or died because Muichiro, before knowing Tanjiro, thought of them as a "low priority"... 😅

Also I have to give props to Tanjiro's sharp and quick mind during a fight. It's truly amazing how creative this kid is and how quickly he grows and gets stronger with every battle. Even his opponents have noticed that and consider him a real threat! That's a huge achievement and I think it would easily lead Tanjiro to become the next Hashira if Muzan wouldn't have been dealt with first. Also, the Kamado siblings team up is always a joy to watch! ☺️

Anyways, I am jumping right into the next volume. I already know what happens, because the events from this arc got animated, but it's still so much fun to read this manga ☺️

La historia se ha puesto muy interesante en este tomo, con un arco que promete volverse incluso más intenso. Y es lo normal. Si el anterior arco ya fue intenso, la cosa solo puede ir a más a partir de ahora, y con mayor motivo cuando nuestros protagonistas se están enfrentando a dos Lunas de nivel superior La atención del lector no puede decaer ni un segundo, ya no solo por el nivel de emoción al que están llegando las peleas y toda la acción, también por la gran cantidad de historias paralelas que entroncan el total del argumento de este volumen.

Si algo hay que reconocerle a Gotouge es que sabe llevar muy bien el ritmo de la narrativa y mantener el equilibrio entre acción y emotividad. Y tampoco hay que olvidar que, aunque parezca una historia shonen ligera y Tanjiro tenga una personalidad tan luminosa y amable y este acompañado de personajes que pueden llegar a ser muy entrañables, cuando toca ponerse dura, la autora se pone dura y no se corta a la hora de darle al lector una pena ración de brutalidad, vísceras y sangre. Véase en este tomo la estatua hecha con partes de los herreros de la aldea por uno de los demonios a abatir. Terrible esa parte, me ha dejado con muy mal cuerpo Sobre todo por la discrepancia entre lo duro y cruel que es y lo cómico de las mascaras que portan aun los herreros.

El personaje de Genya me está gustando. Le veo potencial. Y digo que le veo, porque en este tomo me ha dejado con la sensación de que aún no nos ha mostrado todo lo que puede dar de si. Tiene un buen pasado que explica su forma de ser y sus motivaciones, y una personalidad interesante, amen que su estilo de lucha es especial por que usa armas de fuego en lugar de katana o armas japonesas como la mayoría de personajes. Pero de momento, para mi, le falta algo para ser un personaje que destaque. Espero verlo ya en el tomo número 14. también espero mucho de la Pilar del Amor. No ha tenido oportunidad de lucirse mucho, pero todo llegara.

So, last volume I said that I had mixed feelings regarding Tokito. While I don't adore him like some of the other Hashira, I do like him and am hoping he FUCKING SURVIVES this attack so that I can learn more about him (I swear, Gotouge, if you kill him off...*growls*).

Genya's past was presented in this volume and holy SHIT, this kid's had it rough. I would like to learn more about him and why he fights the way he does, so hopefully more of that will be revealed.

Kanroji was a FUCKING BADASS and her sword is SO FUCKING AWESOME and I FUCKING LOVE HER. That's about all I have to say about that.

Can I just say that I love Nezuko's and Tanjiro's dynamic when fighting? They both prioritize each other's safety and well-being, but also bring out inner strength and push each other further. I wish we had more action series that have this kind of sibling dynamic, it's so awesome and inspiring. Also Nezuko just straight up kicks ass and I love watching her duke it out with demons.

The artwork, specifically the Demon Blood Art, is so awesome and is both beautiful and disturbing. Not that I'm saying the artwork is top tier all the time, but during the fights it really stands out is a feast for the eyes.

Those are my scattered thoughts on this volume, hopefully I can read the next volume close to when it comes out rather than having to wait a FULL MONTH for my order to be fulfilled. Anyways, this was another great volume in a great series.

Still holds up. If I remember correctly this is my favorite volume of this arc. Intense, great fights, and even some "Oh shit is he dead?" type moments because we know Demon Slayer is not scared to kill off big characters. A 4.5 out of 5.

Original Review:

Demon Slayer ramps up this volume as the fight begins.

This volume focuses on Genya and Tanjiro. With both trying their best to fight off one of the big bads we have Muichiro dealing with the demons on the outskirts. With the mist warrior trying his best to return to Genya and Tanjiro they deal with a demon who can keep splitting their body over and over again.

I really enjoyed the intensity of this volume. Both Tanjiro and Genya go full on beast mode to take out this demon. Not only that but have plenty of great surprises and plenty of cliffhangers on this one. This isn't the end of this arc, but the middle piece, and plenty of major things are coming but this action packed volume is great.

Demon Slayer is a rare modern day shonen that I think will be remembered very fondly. Reminds me of Yu Yu Hakusho and Hunter x Hunter where the fights are great but they're great because the characters are! A easy 4.5 out of 5.

My biggest problem with Demon Slayer is probably the repetition. This is the third arc, where the main character goes somewhere with a stronger character. They encounter a very strong enemy, they fight together and then we have result and training. Repeat. I think the characters are great. Everyone feels distinct. They have trauma and it feels that they have a purpose in their lives.

But the way the story is being presented feels framed. And the only factor of surprise is the power-up of the main character. There is the beginning setting. We know our figures and those are our only players, resulting in a small world where lot of conflicts are dealt with Deus ex machina - or some hidden power.

I will be kind and give this four stars but weak four stars.
